Weekly Family Update – 
02.10.26 
Headteacher’s Update: Keeping You Informed About What Matters Most 
What a fantastic week it has been at Abbey College. I continue to be impressed by our 
students’ positive attitude, hard work and commitment to making a difference to both 
themselves and those around them. 
A particular highlight was our Year 6 Open Evening, where we welcomed over 300 families to 
the college. It was wonderful to see so many prospective students and parents exploring our 
school. Our students were exceptional ambassadors, proudly sharing their experiences and 
helping visitors see what makes Abbey College such a special place. 
A special mention must go to Evie in Year 7, who spoke brilliantly about her first four weeks 
at Abbey College. Her confidence, warmth and engaging delivery captivated the audience, 
and she represented the school exceptionally well. She should be incredibly proud of herself 
and has a very bright future ahead. 
I would also like to thank our Parents' Forum for the outstanding support they provide to our 
school community. Their fundraising and commitment have helped us introduce initiatives 
such as our mobile phone pouches and pre-loved uniform shop, both of which have made a 
real difference to families and students. 
The first Parents' Forum meeting of the year will take place on Wednesday 7 October, 
5.00pm-6.00pm, and all parents and carers are warmly invited to attend. Whether you 
would like to get involved regularly or simply find out more, you will be very welcome. The 
Forum's first fundraising event, a Family Quiz Night, will take place on Thursday 12 
November. We hope many families will be able to join us for what promises to be a fun 
evening. 
Have a wonderful weekend. 
Andy Christoforou, Headteacher 

 
Please read on for essential updates. 
Vacancies at Abbey College and across the Meridian Trust 
https://www.abbey.college/vacancies  
Celebration of Spirit - Recognition 
Year 7 Spirit Lunch 
For the first time ever, Year 7 have a 'Spirit Lunch' built into their 
curriculum. Once a fortnight, students come together to build 
their sense of community by sharing lunch, serving one another, 
and engaging in interesting discussion topics. 
This week's question for discussion was: "If you were elected to rule the world for a day, 
what rule would you change?" 

The answers focused on ending discrimination and caring for those less fortunate, responses 
that truly embodied the Abbey College Spirit. 
Headteacher Commendations w/c 28/09/26 
The following students have been awarded with Headteacher's Commendations this week 
for going above and beyond in an area of school life.  They will receive 10 Spirit points and a 
special postcard home. 
 

 
Staff member of the week 
Mr Valentine: Intuition: For taking on a completely different challenge and making a real 
difference with the students. Every day is different in New Horizons, and you just go with it 
and have shown a calm and caring nature towards the students they really respond to. 
Thank you for all your hard work and support to help support them. 
Tell us about something brilliant! 
If you would like to nominate someone for an Abbey College Spirit Award for any out of 
school success stories, then please follow this link or email the Office office@abbey.college. 
Strong Partnerships 
Parent's Forum 
Date for your diary! 
The date of the next Parent's Forum meeting is Wednesday 
7th October 5-6pm. You can either join in person in the 
Boardroom or online via Teams. 
Parent Questionnaire 
Please complete our parent questionnaire to raise any questions you have prior to the next 
meeting. The questionnaire closes on Monday 5th 
October:  https://www.surveymonkey.com/r/ParentsForum26-27 
• Please email ParentsForum@abbey.college any questions.  
• Please find our minutes here: https://www.abbey.college/parents-forum  
• If you would like further information on the Parent's Forum, please email: 
ParentsForum@abbey.college   
Genevieve Wardle - Chair of Parent's Forum 

Uniform Update: Optional Plain Black V-Neck Jumper 
To provide greater flexibility for families whilst maintaining our high uniform standards, 
students may now wear a plain black V-neck jumper under their blazer. 
Please note that: 
• The jumper must be plain black, with no logos, branding, patterns, or 
embellishments. 
• It must be V-necked to allow the school tie and shirt collar to remain visible. 
• Hoodies, sweatshirts, crew-neck jumpers, or knitwear in other colours are not 
permitted. 
• The jumper must be worn underneath the blazer, not as an alternative to it. 
Family Quiz Night! 
The Abbey College Parents' Forum invites families to a fun-filled Family Quiz Night on 
Thursday 12th November in the South Hall. 
Gather a team of up to six people, test your knowledge, and compete for prizes, all while 
supporting a great cause. Every penny raised will go towards exciting new opportunities and 
resources for Abbey College students. 
 

Up-to-date MCAS details 
Please ensure that your contact details are kept up to date on MCAS (MyChildAtSchool). 
Having the correct information helps us contact you quickly if needed and ensures you 
receive important school communications. 
You can update your details yourself at any time through the MCAS app or website. 
Alternatively, if you need assistance, please email office@abbey.college with your updated 
information. 
Zebra Crossing location Survey 
The County Council would like feedback on a proposed Zebra Crossing location near the 
school. Please complete the survey here: https://yourvoice.cambridgeshire.gov.uk/place-
and-sustainability/ramsey-zebra-crossing-feedback/ 
Any queries, please contact Hanane Rouadi, Assistant Project Manager, Local Improvements 
Team, Hanane.Rouadi@cambridgeshire.gov.uk 
Diary Dates  
 
Everything You Need to Know About Assessments 
 

Ensuring Pupils Feel Safe and Behave Well 
Safety First 
Worries 
Students discussed emotional wellbeing and the importance of talking about worries early. 
They were reminded of the support available in school and encouraged to seek help if they 
are struggling. 
Useful Resources 
• YoungMinds: https://www.youngminds.org.uk/parent 
• Anna Freud: https://www.annafreud.org/parents-and-carers 
• Place2Be: https://parentingsmart.place2be.org.uk 
• NHS Every Mind Matters: https://www.nhs.uk/every-mind-matters 
If you need support or have any concerns about your child's wellbeing or safety, please 
contact welfare@abbey.college 
Promoting Positive Behaviour Every Day 
Student attendance  
Week 4 – Impact on Wellbeing  
Being in school supports more than just your learning—it supports your wellbeing too.  
Routine, friendships, and feeling part of your community all help you feel positive and 
confident.  
Coming in matters for your mind as well as your grades.  

Supporting Your Child’s Wider Development 
Offer & Opportunity Programme (OOPs) - Autumn Term 
 
 

 
Student curriculum 
How can I find out what my child is learning in each subject? 
Discover Our Curriculum 
At Abbey College, we want every student to feel challenged, supported and inspired to 
achieve their best. Our broad and balanced curriculum combines excellent teaching, rich 
experiences and strong careers guidance to help young people thrive both in school and 
beyond. 
Our curriculum is designed around three simple aims: helping students understand the 
wider world, providing an ambitious education for all, and ensuring that every learner has 
the opportunity to succeed. Parents can explore what is taught across Key Stages 3, 4 and 5, 
along with information about homework, higher-attaining students and relationships 
education. 
Find out more: View our Curriculum Overview 
Communicating with us and raising concerns 
Click here to access this Communication Flowchart on our website. 
Parent Friendly Policy Guide: 
https://www.abbey.college/key-policies--reports  
Other news updates can be found here: 
• Our news page: https://www.abbey.college/school-communications  
• Facebook: https://www.facebook.com/pg/RamseyAbbeyCollege/posts/  
• Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/abbeycollege_ramsey/

Weekly Family Update - 09.10.26 
Headteacher’s Update: Keeping You Informed About What Matters 
Most 
Thank you for your continued support in helping your child attend school every day. Regular 
attendance is one of the most important factors in a young person's success, wellbeing and 
sense of belonging at school. 
Every lesson matters. Being in school each day helps students build strong relationships, 
develop confidence, keep up with learning and make the most of the opportunities available 
to them. Even missing occasional days can make it harder for students to stay connected to 
their learning. 
As we approach the half-term break, we would be grateful for your support in ensuring 
students attend every day until the end of term. Students finish for half term on Thursday 22 
October. 
Please note that the following are Meridian Trust INSET days, when students are not in 
school: 
• Friday 23 October 
• Monday 2 November 
This means students will have an extended break before returning to school on Tuesday 3 
November, giving plenty of time to rest and recharge. 
Thank you for working with us to ensure students are in school, on time, every day. Your 
support makes a real difference. 
Every day in school is a day of learning, friendship and opportunity. 
Andy Christoforou, Headteacher 

 
Please read on for essential updates. 
Vacancies at Abbey College and across the Meridian Trust 
https://www.abbey.college/vacancies  
Celebration of Spirit - Recognition 
 

Headteacher Commendations w/c 05/10/26 
The following students have been awarded with Headteacher's Commendations this week 
for going above and beyond in an area of school life.  They will receive 10 Spirit points and a 
special postcard home. 

 

 
Staff member of the week 
Miss Andrew-Martin: Passion - Your love for creative writing is infectious. To have 30 
students regularly attending an OOP and being so proud of the work they produce there is 
wonderful to see. Thank you for being so willing to give up your time to allow students to 
feel such a sense of pride and belonging. 
Tell us about something brilliant! 

If you would like to nominate someone for an Abbey College Spirit Award for any out of 
school success stories, then please follow this link or email the Office office@abbey.college . 
Strong Partnerships 
Parent's Forum 
Parent's Forum Update 
At last night’s Parent's Forum meeting, Mrs Noble provided an overview of the changes to 
the Relationships and Sex Education (RSE) guidance and invited feedback from parents. If 
you would like to contribute, please submit any comments here:  
• Relationships, Sex and Health Education: Parent Consultation – Fill in form.  
We look forward to using your feedback to help shape our updated policy, which will be 
published next year. 
We also continued planning for our exciting fundraising quiz on 12th November, and 
preparations are well underway. 
At our next Parent's Forum meeting, Miss Lane will provide an update on how our new Year 
7 students are settling into life at Abbey College and we will look at some projects to donate 
funds to. 
• Please email ParentsForum@abbey.college any questions.  
• Please find our minutes here: https://www.abbey.college/parents-forum  
• If you would like further information on the Parent's Forum, please email: 
ParentsForum@abbey.college   
Genevieve Wardle - Chair of Parent's Forum 
Family Quiz Night! 
The Abbey College Parents' Forum invites families to a fun-filled Family Quiz Night on 
Thursday 12th November in the South Hall. 
Gather a team of up to six people for £6 per team, test your knowledge, and compete for 
prizes, all while supporting a great cause.  
There are prizes which have been donated for a raffle on the night.    

The sixth form will be running the quiz so any support would be much appreciated! 
Every penny raised will go towards exciting new opportunities and resources for Abbey 
College students. 
 
Up-to-date MCAS details 
Please ensure that your contact details are kept up to date on MCAS (MyChildAtSchool). 
Having the correct information helps us contact you quickly if needed and ensures you 
receive important school communications. 

You can update your details yourself at any time through the MCAS app or website. 
Alternatively, if you need assistance, please email office@abbey.college with your updated 
information. 
Road Safety 
 
Zebra Crossing location Survey 
The County Council would like feedback on a proposed Zebra Crossing location near the 
school. Please complete the survey here: https://yourvoice.cambridgeshire.gov.uk/place-
and-sustainability/ramsey-zebra-crossing-feedback/ 
Any queries, please contact Hanane Rouadi, Assistant Project Manager, Local Improvements 
Team, Hanane.Rouadi@cambridgeshire.gov.uk 
Diary Dates  
 
��� Inset Days Coming Up 
Please note that the following are Meridian Trust-wide Inset Days. All Meridian Trust 
schools, including Abbey College, will be closed to students on these dates: 
������������ Friday 23 October 
������������Monday 2 November 

������������Friday 27 November 
���� Please add these dates to your family calendar. 
These training days allow staff from across Meridian Trust to work together, share best 
practice and continue to improve the education we provide for all students. 
Everything You Need to Know About Assessments 
 
Ensuring Pupils Feel Safe and Behave Well 
Safety First 
Healthy Habits 
This week students discussed healthy habits, hygiene, hydration, sleep and self-care. 
We encouraged students to consider how everyday health habits support both wellbeing 
and school attendance. 
Useful Resources 
• NHS Live Well: https://www.nhs.uk/live-well 
• NHS Better Health: https://www.nhs.uk/better-health 
• The Sleep Charity: https://thesleepcharity.org.uk 
If you need support or have any concerns about your child's wellbeing or safety, please 
contact welfare@abbey.college 
Promoting Positive Behaviour Every Day 
Student attendance  
Week 5 – Coughs & Colds  

It’s okay to feel under the weather sometimes—but most coughs and colds don’t need days 
off school.  
If you’re well enough, being in school helps you stay on track.  
Don’t let a small illness lead to big gaps in learning.  
Ms Davis – Attendance Officer 
Supporting Your Child’s Wider Development 
Offer & Opportunity Programme (OOPs) - Autumn Term 
 

 
 
 
Click here 
Student curriculum 
How can I find out what my child is learning in each subject? 
Learning outside the classroom (LoTC) 
At Abbey College, we believe learning should extend beyond the classroom. Through a wide 
range of opportunities, students can experience art, culture, heritage, adventure and the 
natural world, helping to broaden their horizons and build confidence. These enriching 
experiences are offered through our curriculum and our Offer and Opportunity Programme 
(OOP), alongside trips, visits and activities such as the Combined Cadet Force (CCF). The aim 
is to give every student access to memorable experiences that support their personal growth 
and development.  
Find out more: Learning Outside the Classroom 
Communicating with us and raising concerns 
Click here to access this Communication Flowchart on our website. 

Parent Friendly Policy Guide: 
https://www.abbey.college/key-policies--reports  
Other news updates can be found here: 
• Our news page: https://www.abbey.college/school-communications  
• Facebook: https://www.facebook.com/pg/RamseyAbbeyCollege/posts/  
• Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/abbeycollege_ramsey/

Original 8 series of classic 90s comedy show gets new streaming location in the UK
metadata.contentSnippet: Fans can now enjoy Red Dwarf's entire original run, with all eight seasons from 1988 to 1999 now streaming on Netflix in the UK.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Original 8 series of classic 90s comedy show gets new streaming location in the UK
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A cult sci-fi comedy has landed on Netflix in the UK, bringing a fresh wave of nostalgia to screens. Fans can now enjoy Red Dwarf's entire original run, with all eight seasons from 1988 to 1999 now streaming on the platform. The streaming service revealed the news on social media, with the message: "Attention smegheads!" Attention, smegheads! Seasons 1-8 of RED DWARF are now on @NetflixUK. https://t.co/BFTys2IXP5 — Netflix UK & Ireland (@NetflixUK) October 28, 2026 Red Dwarf follows the misadventures of Dave Lister (Craig Charles), the last known human alive, who wakes up three million years in the future aboard a mining spaceship. He is joined by a motley crew including a hologram of his former bunkmate Arnold Rimmer (Chris Barrie), the evolved humanoid Cat (Danny John-Jules), and the well-meaning service mechanoid Kryten (Robert Llewellyn). The series originally aired on BBC Two and later returned for additional seasons and specials between 2009 and 2020, totalling 12 seasons and a feature-length special, The Promised Land. Beyond the small screen, Red Dwarf has inspired audiobooks, novels, and graphic novels. This year, long-time co-creator Rob Grant died, with his final project, prequel novel Red Dwarf: Titan, alongside collaborator Andrew Marshall, released posthumously in July. The book explores the early lives of Lister and Rimmer and sets the stage for the events of the series. Mr Grant described the plot, saying the duo "get a message from the far future warning them that all realities are going to collapse unless they do something about it." Plans for a new TV special were cancelled in 2025, but Doug Naylor, who co-created the show with Mr Grant, has said he continues to write scripts set in the Red Dwarf universe. The show remains available on BBC iPlayer. In other TV news, after 36 years on Sky One in the UK, The Simpsons is set to disappear from Sky screens. The long-running animated series, which has had a 36-year partnership with Sky in the UK, will be dropped from the channel from November 1, marking the end of a decades-long broadcast tradition. This change follows Sky's loss of the rights to newer episodes, which have been available exclusively on Disney+ in the UK since 2023. In December 2024, it was announced new episodes of The Simpsons would air exclusively on Disney+, followed by E4, although Sky continued to show classic episodes from earlier seasons. Wesley Mead, a TV blogger, said: "Sky One’s repeats have continued in earnest throughout 2025 and 2026." They remained the only place to see seasons 34 and 35—the final two seasons to predate the E4 deal—on broadcast TV; they also retained rights to broadcast a number of classic seasons. A spokesperson for Sky confirmed that from the end of October, Sky One will no longer feature previous series of The Simpsons in its schedule. Recommended reading: On October 31, Sky One will air a final Treehouse of Horror repeat at 6pm before the show is dropped from the schedule for two weeks. Mr Mead said this was the first such break since the early 1990s. Despite the loss, Sky customers with the Ultimate TV package will still be able to watch The Simpsons through Disney+. What is your favourite show on Netflix? Let us know in the comments.

metadata.title: Aldi supersize White Company candle dupes are back – £70 cheaper than the real thing
metadata.contentSnippet: Aldi is bringing back its popular Christmas candles, with prices starting at £5.99 and shoppers able to save up to £70 compared with posh White Company version.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Aldi supersize White Company candle dupes are back – £70 cheaper than the real thing
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Aldi is bringing back its popular Christmas inclusion candles, with prices starting at £5.99 and shoppers able to save up to £70 compared with The White Company. The budget supermarket's statement candles will return to stores nationwide from Sunday, November 1, just in time for shoppers looking for affordable Christmas gifts and festive home decorations. The range comes in three sizes, with the largest weighing a hefty 4.5kg and offering up to 200 hours of burn time. Each candle is available in two festive-inspired fragrances – Winter Spice and Scandinavian Forest – and features dried fruit, berries and cinnamon sticks encased in the wax for a decorative finish. The range comes in three sizes, with the largest weighing a hefty 4.5kg (Image: Aldi) Aldi says its candles offer savings of up to 83% compared with selected alternatives from The White Company, making them a tempting option for shoppers who want a luxury-looking home accessory without the designer price tag. Weighing 4.5kg, Aldi's largest candle is designed to make a statement, with multiple wicks and an impressive 200-hour burn time. The smallest option offers a more affordable way to try the trend, with a 660g candle promising up to 60 hours of burn time. The rectangular design is intended for display on dining tables, mantelpieces and festive arrangements, with a 1kg size and up to 100 hours of burn time. Recommended reading: The Inclusion Candle range will be available in Aldi stores nationwide from Sunday, November 1, while stocks last. With prices starting below £6, the candles could appeal to shoppers looking for an affordable Christmas present or a festive addition to their own home. However, the products are available in stores only, and shoppers may need to move quickly if previous demand for Aldi's popular homeware ranges is anything to go by. What's your favourite dupe? Tell us in the comments below...

metadata.title: Starbucks brings back Red Cups – and launches a festive first for Christmas 2026
metadata.contentSnippet: Starbucks UK unveils its 2026 Christmas menu, with Red Cups, a Holiday Cold Cup, new peppermint drinks and festive food. See the full menu and prices.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Starbucks brings back Red Cups – and launches a festive first for Christmas 2026
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Red cups are on their way back to Starbucks, alongside Peppermint drinks, a Christmas menu of old favourites and new discoveries - and its first-ever Holiday Cold Cup. The coffee giant is bringing back its much-loved iconic Red Cups from 5 November, alongside Sticky Toffee Pecan Cake, Chocolate Orange Cake Cube, Red Velvet Scroll, Christmas Tree Brownie and Reindeer Cake Pops. This year's menu sees peppermint take centre stage, with an entire range of new drinks inspired by the flavour's popularity in the US. From a Peppermint Mocha topped with crunchy peppermint sugar sprinkles to a chilled matcha creation finished with white chocolate cold foam, there's plenty to tempt those looking for a little festive indulgence. And, of course, some familiar favourites are making their return, including the Gingerbread Latte, Toffee Nut Latte and Eggnog Latte. The new Starbucks Christmas menu (Image: Starbucks) For many coffee fans, the arrival of Starbucks' Red Cups marks the unofficial start of the Christmas season. From 5 November, the recognisable festive cups will return across participating UK stores, giving seasonal coffee runs a familiar splash of red. This year, however, there's a new addition to the line-up. Starbucks is introducing its first-ever Holiday Cold Cup, offering a festive option for customers who prefer iced coffees and Frappuccino blended drinks to steaming hot lattes. Whether you're picking up a warming seasonal coffee on the way to work or treating yourself to an iced drink during a Christmas shopping trip, the new cups are designed to bring a little festive spirit to every order. The new Starbucks Christmas menu (Image: Starbucks) Peppermint is the headline flavour this year, with four new creations joining the seasonal line-up. Starbucks Rewards members can get an exclusive First Taste of the drinks from 29 October, ahead of the nationwide festive menu launch on 5 November. The new drinks include: The range offers a new way to enjoy peppermint beyond the classic chocolate pairing, with the iced matcha bringing a different flavour combination to the festive menu. Sweet treats on the new Starbucks Christmas menu (Image: Starbucks) Not ready to swap your usual festive favourite? Several familiar seasonal drinks are returning, including the sweet, nutty Toffee Nut Latte and warming Gingerbread Latte. The returning drinks menu includes: Customers can also upgrade any espresso-based drink, including a latte or Americano, to Starbucks Christmas Blend. The seasonal coffee features Arabica beans with notes of herbs and baking spices, finished with a rich chocolate flavour. The new Starbucks Christmas menu (Image: Starbucks) It's not just the drinks getting a festive makeover. Starbucks is also bringing new cakes, brownies and sweet treats to its food counter, alongside savoury options packed with traditional Christmas flavours. The festive food range launches from 5 November. Reindeers on the new Starbucks Christmas menu (Image: Starbucks) For those after something more substantial than a sweet treat, Starbucks is also bringing back its festive savoury favourites, alongside a new flatbread. Recommended reading: There's a little wait for most customers, although Starbucks Rewards members can get an early taste of the new peppermint drinks. Starbucks Rewards First Taste begins today, with selected festive beverages available exclusively to members in participating stores and through the Starbucks UK app. The full Holiday menu launches nationwide, including the returning Red Cups and the first-ever Holiday Cold Cup, arrives on November 5.

metadata.title: 'Dangerous driving' arrest after motorcyclist dies in crash with car
metadata.contentSnippet: A man has been arrested after a motorcyclist died in a crash involving a car on Elton Road near Wansford.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: 'Dangerous driving' arrest after motorcyclist dies in crash with car
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A man has been arrested after a motorcyclist died in a crash involving a car. The collision happened on Elton Road, near Wansford, at around 7.15pm on Wednesday (October 28). Emergency services including the air ambulance rushed to the incident, which involved a black Ford Mustang Mac-E and the motorcycle. The man riding the motorcycle received serious injuries and died at the scene. A 27-year-old man from Peterborough who was driving the Ford received minor injuries and was taken to hospital for treatment. He has since been arrested on suspicion of causing death by dangerous driving and remains in custody. Police are keen to speak to anyone who witnessed the collision, particularly the driver of another vehicle that is believed to have been travelling ahead of the Ford. Those with information should contact police online, quoting Operation Barn or incident 527 of 28 October. Those without internet access should call 101. Have you got a story you want to share? Get in touch at oliver.murphy@newsquest.co.uk

metadata.title: Local government shakeup in Cambridgeshire slammed as ‘gut punch’
metadata.contentSnippet: A planned local government shakeup in Cambridgeshire and Peterborough has been slammed as a “merry-go-round” as the plans face further delays.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Local government shakeup in Cambridgeshire slammed as ‘gut punch’
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary:
A planned local government shakeup has been slammed as a “merry-go-round” as the plans face further delays. Local councils in Cambridgeshire and Peterborough were set to be dissolved in government plans for local government reorganisation (LGR). They were set to be replaced with a number of unitary councils which would handle both county and district level responsibilities. An announcement on what form this would take was expected in July, but the Secretary of State for Local Government at the time, Steve Reed, delayed the decision until October. At the time, he said the “shadow elections” planned for May 2027 for the newly-created authorities would still take place. But in September, the government said local elections would go ahead for Peterborough, East Cambridgeshire, Fenland and Cambridge City in 2027. South Cambridgeshire and Huntingdonshire already held their elections in May. All six councils and Cambridgeshire County Council were set to be replaced with two or three bigger councils under the plans, with the shadow elections setting the stage for a transition the next year. Currently, lower-tier district councils look after things like bin collections, leisure facilities and council tax, while the upper-tier county council is responsible for road maintenance, public health and education, including special educational needs and disabilities. Today, it was announced that the transition would face a further delay. Jim McMahon MP, Parliamentary Under-Secretary of State for Local Government, Devolution and Regional Growth, announced in Parliament that only five of the 14 areas under review would be proceeding. These are East Sussex and Brighton and Hove, Gloucestershire, Oxfordshire and Warwickshire and Worcestershire. He said: “To be clear, all options and proposals in these areas will remain under consideration and I will approach all decisions with an open mind. “As such it should not be assumed the same proposal will automatically
  be selected. It is important the process is allowed to run its course and allow full and proper consideration.” To help with the “costs of uncertainty” he said all areas would receive half of transition funding – £450k per new unitary previously announced and £500k for each area in Cambridgeshire and Peterborough and West Sussex. He said there would be a further update by Christmas and every area will have outcomes by early next year. Pippa Heylings, Liberal Democrat MP for South Cambridgeshire, said: “Local Government Reorganisation has become a merry-go-round of changing decisions. “First, we were promised elections in May 2027. Then the decision for Cambridgeshire and West Sussex was delayed, while ministers still insisted elections would go ahead in May 2027. “Just two months later, the whole scheme was put on hold. Now it’s back, with a new date of 2028. Businesses need certainty to invest and plan. “Councils need certainty to set budgets and invest in our communities. the electorate deserve a clear and transparent process and council staff deserve certainty about their jobs and their families’ futures. “Instead, they’ve had shambolic U-turns and no certainty whatsoever. “Business owners across South Cambridgeshire have told me how badly this uncertainty has hurt them, putting their businesses at risk when they could least afford it. “Today’s delay is another gut-punch to Cambridgeshire’s businesses and councils, and it does nothing to solve the uncertainty that has plagued this whole process. “How can businesses and council leaders trust that we won’t be back here in a couple of months facing yet another delay? “I’ll keep pressing the Government until our communities get the certainty they deserve.” Leader of Cambridgeshire County Council, Councillor Lucy Nethsingha, said: “This is a bitter disappointment and once again shows we have a Government incapable of making decisions or following through on its own policies. “Cambridgeshire and Peterborough were already stuck in ‘LGR limbo’ and to simply extend that further beggars believe. “Continued uncertainty simply creates increased risks, prevents us from making long-term plans and all at a time when the demand for and the costs of providing council services are rising. “In particular, the anxiety and uncertainty that this creates for the hard-working staff in the seven councils in this area is intolerable. “We risk being unable to retain and recruit good people, we risk being unable to plan financially over the longer term and we risk being forced into making more short-term procurement and contract decisions, all because this Government can’t get its act together. “Our residents and communities deserve better; our staff deserve better and the democratically elected councillors across this area deserve better. “This Government may have changed Prime Minister, but it remains firmly mired in chaos. “Yes, decisions have consequences, but indecision, dither and delay also has consequences, in this case for local public services, the people we employ and the people who rely on us. “Despite this further indecision, we will remain our focussed upon delivering our services for residents and communities and doing the very best for Cambridgeshire, while once again waiting on the Government.”

metadata.title: Cambridgeshire firms left with ‘more questions than answers’ after Budget
metadata.contentSnippet: Business leaders say the latest Budget offers "more questions than answers" for firms across Cambridgeshire.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Cambridgeshire firms left with ‘more questions than answers’ after Budget
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Business leaders say the latest Budget offers "more questions than answers" for firms across Cambridgeshire. The Cambridgeshire Chamber of Commerce has welcomed some of the Chancellor’s announcements, including changes to business rates and investment plans, but criticised the lack of support on employer National Insurance contributions, energy costs, and export provision. Charlotte Horobin, chief executive of the Cambridgeshire Chamber of Commerce, said: "The Budget leaves many businesses in Cambridgeshire, Peterborough and Stamford with more questions than answers. "The business-rates threshold increase is a step in the right direction but falls short of what the British Chambers of Commerce called for. "The absence of employer NIC relief, business energy support and export provision means the short-term pressures most businesses are facing remain largely unaddressed." Charlotte said the real impact of the Budget will depend on how quickly the measures translate into tangible benefits. She said: "There are encouraging signals on place-based growth and devolution, but the practical test is simple: how quickly will these measures translate into lower operating costs, stronger investment and real opportunities for businesses on the ground?" The Budget includes a rise in the small business rate relief threshold from £12,000 to £18,000, removing rates for 70,000 more businesses and freezing business rates for two years. Other measures include a 3.9 per cent increase in the National Living Wage and National Minimum Wage, a tripled trading allowance, and a new entrepreneur’s allowance intended to cover a year of living costs. The Chancellor also announced a scale-up programme for female founders, new founders’ Capital Gains Tax relief, and a fiscal devolution roadmap to expand local powers for mayoral authorities, and referenced the Cambridge Development Corporation. Funding for a local apprenticeship service was also included, alongside a plan that fully funds the defence investment plan and a new defence spending taskforce.

metadata.title: Cambridgeshire welcomes new tax powers to tackle 1,800km of sinking roads
metadata.contentSnippet: Cambridgeshire County Council has welcomed new tax powers announced by the Chancellor during the Budget.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Cambridgeshire welcomes new tax powers to tackle 1,800km of sinking roads
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Cambridgeshire County Council has welcomed new tax powers announced by the Chancellor during the Budget. Councillor Lucy Nethsingha, leader of Cambridgeshire County Council, described the move as a positive step toward greater local control. Cllr Nethsingha said: "We welcome the Chancellor’s decision to devolve tax powers. "Liberal Democrats have long argued that decisions about local investment should be made here in Cambridgeshire and Peterborough, not in Whitehall, and this is a welcome step in the right direction." She emphasised the potential impact on long-standing infrastructure issues in the region. Cllr Nethsingha said: "With that new capacity comes a real opportunity to tackle one of the biggest infrastructure problems in our county. "Around 40% of Cambridgeshire sits on peat and other weak soils, and more than 1,800km of our roads are built on ground that shifts, cracks and sinks." She called on the Mayor to direct some of the Combined Authority’s expanded borrowing capacity toward longer-term solutions. Cllr Nethsingha also urged central government to ensure councils are properly funded for the responsibilities they are expected to deliver.

metadata.title: We watched 700 drones transform racecourse sky with chameleon and space scenes
metadata.contentSnippet: A dazzling drone display lit up the night sky at Newmarket Racecourse, captivating thousands of spectators.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: We watched 700 drones transform racecourse sky with chameleon and space scenes
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A dazzling drone display lit up the sky at Newmarket Racecourse, captivating thousands of spectators. The show, held on the Rowley Mile and organised by Immersive Drone Lightshows, featured 700 illuminated drones forming vibrant shapes and animations in the night sky. A delayed start due to technical issues meant families were treated to extra entertainment, including a second set from a live musician and animal noise guessing games led by the compère. A moment from the Space Safari drone show at Newmarket Racecourse (Image: Newsquest) The display began by 8pm with a cinematic voiceover from BAFTA award-winning TV presenter Michaela Strachan introducing the story. It combined storytelling, music, and environmental messages, encouraging audiences to protect wildlife. A standout moment came when the drones formed a lifelike chameleon, drawing audible gasps from the crowd. The show moved from safari scenes to outer space, featuring rockets, ships, and satellites—an imaginative way to keep younger viewers engaged and entertained. A moment from the Space Safari drone show at Newmarket Racecourse (Image: Newsquest)

metadata.title: Two taken to hospital after crash as Cambs motorway closed
metadata.contentSnippet: Two people have been taken to hospital after a crash on the M11 near Girton, Cambridge.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Two taken to hospital after crash as Cambs motorway closed
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Two people have been taken to hospital after a crash on a motorway in Cambridgeshire. Police were called at about 11.10am today (Thursday October 29) with reports of a collision involving multiple vehicles on the southbound carriageway of the M11 near Girton. A spokesperson for Cambridgeshire Constabulary said: "“A second minor collision took place shortly afterwards on the opposite carriageway." Emergency services attended the scene, and the road was closed in both directions. An East of England Ambulance Service spokesperson said: “We were called just before 11.15am to a road traffic collision on the southbound M11 near Girton. "Three ambulances, an ambulance officer vehicle, two vehicles from the Hazardous Area Response Team and the Magpas Air Ambulance were sent to the scene. "Two patients were transported by road to Addenbrooke’s Hospital for further treatment." National Highways reported an air ambulance attended the scene.

Becky Hill will headline a major show in 2027 as part of the popular Newmarket Nights concert series. metadata.title: Cambs disability charity marks 35 years after securing £1.32m for clients
metadata.contentSnippet: A disability support charity in Cambridgeshire is celebrating 35 years of service.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Cambs disability charity marks 35 years after securing £1.32m for clients
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A disability support charity in Cambridgeshire is celebrating 35 years of service. The Disability Information Services Hub (DISH) began as a helpline in 1991 and now supports people across Huntingdonshire, Fenland and South Cambridgeshire with information, advice and help applying for disability-related benefits. In 2025/26 alone, DISH received 779 referrals and helped clients secure more than £1.32 million in welfare support. Tracy Hyland, chief executive of DISH, said: "DISH began with a simple purpose: to help people living with a disability find the information and support they need. "As we celebrate our 35th anniversary, I am proud that our small organisation now supports more people than ever while working alongside dedicated community partners." Client and caseworker (Image: DISH) To mark the milestone, DISH has released an anniversary booklet highlighting its three decades of service, available on its website and social media channels. Ms Hyland said: "This milestone is more than a date: it represents the thousands of people we have supported and the strength of our community. "Our charity has adapted, innovated, and grown to meet many challenges head-on. "This anniversary reflects the dedication of our staff and volunteers, the governance of our board, and the commitment of our partners and supporters." Gethyn Williams, chair of trustees at DISH, said: "DISH takes systems that can feel complicated and intimidating and makes them easier to navigate, one person at a time. "We combine expert advice with kindness and personal attention, and that is why people trust us." Service users have also expressed their appreciation for the charity’s support. One client, Madge, said: "The main problem I had was I couldn’t see the form due to my eyesight. "DISH was so helpful with the form filling, because they came to my home, which made things much easier for me to complete the form. "DISH was there to help me, and I’m so grateful."

metadata.title: Former Cambs councillor and cadet leader guilty of rape and child sexual offences
metadata.contentSnippet: Former Peterborough City Councillor and Army Cadet Force leader Rylan Ray has been found guilty of rape and multiple child sexual offences.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Former Cambs councillor and cadet leader guilty of rape and child sexual offences
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A former Cambridgeshire councillor and Army Cadet Force leader has been found guilty of rape and multiple child sexual offences. Rylan Ray, 26, from Westgate, Peterborough, was convicted of 23 offences following a 24-day trial at Ipswich Crown Court. The former Peterborough City Councillor had already pleaded guilty to three other offences before the trial began. Ray used his role as a detachment commander in the Army Cadet Force (ACF) to contact young people on WhatsApp under the guise of discussing cadet duties. He then encouraged them to move conversations to Snapchat, where the messaging became sexual. Ray created a fake Snapchat account posing as a teenage girl named Chelsie to obtain intimate images from his victims. He was linked to the account after a phone call from one victim to Chelsie was answered by Ray. Another fake account was traced to his flat through its IP address. Photos of Chelsie, including the Snapchat icon, were found on Ray’s phone, along with intimate images from six victims that had only been sent to the fake accounts. He also told a 16-year-old cadet that he could get him into clubs without ID because he was a Peterborough licensing officer. Rylan Ray was a former Peterborough City Councillor (Image: Cambridgeshire Police) The offences, involving 11 victims, came to light in 2025 after two 16th birthday parties were held at Ray’s home. The parties were attended mostly by cadets or people connected to the ACF. Parents raised concerns about drinking and behaviour at the parties, prompting complaints to the ACF. When officers spoke to children who attended the parties, several disclosed sexual messaging with Ray. He was also involved with the Combined Cadet Force (CCF) at Stanground Academy and Nene Park Academy in Peterborough. Police were notified in May 2025 and launched an investigation, where some children reported not only sexual messages but also sexual assault. Ray was arrested that same month. In a prepared statement during his police interview, he admitted he "may have" engaged in inappropriate conversations but denied any sexual motivation. He said he was "truly shocked and disgusted" by the allegations and claimed they had "ruined his career." He then gave no further comment. In later interviews, Ray admitted receiving topless images from one child and acknowledged that some messages were sexual in nature. He also admitted sending a photo of his genitals and pornography to the same boy. Ray was charged with 25 offences. Following media coverage of the charges, another victim came forward and reported that Ray had raped him after a night out in Peterborough in 2019. Before the trial, Ray pleaded guilty to two counts of causing or inciting a boy aged 13 to 15 to engage in sexual activity and one count of causing a child aged 13 to 15 to look at an image of sexual activity. During the trial, he admitted two further offences of making indecent images of children. He was found guilty of 23 additional offences, including rape, sexual assault, and sexual communication with a child. Ray will be sentenced at Ipswich Crown Court on January 8. Detective Constable Gordon Logan, who investigated, said: "The roles Ray held allowed him trusted access to young people, and he seized these opportunities to abuse them sexually. "We would like to praise the bravery of the children involved in confiding in others what had happened to them. "Doing so takes a lot of courage but it was so important that they did, because we then began investigating. "Many of the victims involved felt they had no choice but to engage in the chats with Ray. "In an increasingly digital world, mobile phones and social media mean children can be vulnerable to those who prey on their innocence and exploit their trust. "We encourage all members of the public to be aware of adults who pay an unusual amount of attention to a child – no matter their profession. "Sharing any concerns, no matter how small, can make all the difference."

metadata.title: Hunts dog lover's event sees 300 labradors gather at Jeremy Clarkson’s pub
metadata.contentSnippet: More than 600 people, including Jeremy Clarkson's wife Lisa Hogan, attended a labrador meet-up organised by a dog lover from Godmanchester.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Hunts dog lover's event sees 300 labradors gather at Jeremy Clarkson’s pub
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: More than 600 people, including Jeremy Clarkson's wife Lisa Hogan, attended a labrador meet-up organised by a Huntingdonshire dog lover. Godmanchester dog lover Michael Singer organised the fox-red Labrador event at Jeremy Clarkson’s pub The Farmer's Dog in Oxfordshire. His first meet at the pub in 2024 attracted 179 labradors, but this year's saw more than 300 - plus 600 human visitors. Lisa Hogan, Jeremy Clarkson’s partner, also attended. Michael (right), his wife Kerrie (centre), and Lisa Hogan (left) (Image: Michael Singer) Mr Singer said: “The whole thing started as a bit of a joke, really. "I wanted an excuse to visit Jeremy Clarkson’s pub, so I said to my partner: ‘Shall I organise a Fox Red Labrador meet there?’ “The reason for organising the second meet was just as simple — I’d run out of Hawkstone cider and needed an excuse to go back!" Michael said the event started as a bit of a joke (Image: Michael Singer) A portion of the money raised through ticket sales will be going to Shout, helping support farmers’ mental health. Mr Singer said: "It’s fantastic that an event bringing so many people and dogs together can also contribute to such an important cause." A portion of the money raised will be going to Shout (Image: Michael Singer) He said more than 1,000 people contacted him about tickets before the event, which sold out. Messages have continued since, with people asking when another meet will take place. Mr Singer said: “Joking aside, it’s been an absolutely brilliant day. "Yes, it rained, but nobody seemed to care. "Everyone turned up, the dogs had a fantastic time, and the atmosphere was amazing. "I never imagined that a simple idea would grow into something this big.”

metadata.title: Council approves plan to convert historic former school into home
metadata.contentSnippet: The Old Day School in Bluntisham High Street will now be turned into a three-bed house after lying empty for around five years.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Council approves plan to convert historic former school into home
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Find, save and share Public Notices that affect you in the  area. The Public Notice Portal carries statutory public notices published in local newspapers and is the fastest and most effective way of finding out what is happening in YOUR neighbourhood. A historic former school is set to get a new lease of life after fears it would be lost forever. The Old Day School in Bluntisham High Street will now be turned into a three-bed house after lying empty for around five years. Huntingdonshire District Council’s planning officers recommended the proposal be refused as it would cause “substantial” harm to the Grade II listed building. This was due to the dividing of the school hall to allow for a third bedroom, but residents submitted 17 letters in support of the plans. Philippa Hope, of Bluntisham Parish Council, told the council’s development management committee the building “needs to be preserved”. She said: “It has a resonance for the people of Bluntisham – and is integral to the spirit of place. “However, it is no longer a school and could never be used as a school again. “To convert any building into a home internal changes are inevitable – the school building is the same and any changes are justifiable in securing the long-term future of this vacant listed building.” A previous proposal was refused in 2025 despite concerns that the building hasn’t been properly maintained since it stopped being used as a school in 1968. Councillors had concerns with the proposed rear extension which was reduced in size in the resubmission, with the hall division the last remaining concern for officers. Simon Claridge, the applicant, told the committee he cares “deeply about the building” which had continued to “deteriorate through vandalism, broken windows, water ingress, roof damage and even attempted arson”. He said: “We’ve listened, compromised and repeatedly amended our proposals. Given the resources already invested though – this really is our last attempt to save this building. “Every year that passes more of the very heritage we’re trying to protect is lost. “I understand the conservation’s desire to retain the school hall as one open space – however, a completely open hall simply does not provide a practical family home.” He added that the partition would be “reversible” as a “further compromise” and the proposal was the “only way of ensuring that this building will continue to stand”. Cllr Paul Hodgson-Jones, speaking as ward councillor for Holywell-cum-Needingworth, said the school hall would “not be open to the public to see”. The Conservative councillor said: “They will still be able to see that it’s an old school hall from the outside because it’s evident from the architecture.” Cllr Julie Kerr agreed that the hall would be too big for a room in a home of that size and couldn’t be maintained “as a viable room”. The independent councillor said: “The person who owns it is clearly passionate about the building, he lives next door, he cares about it, he cares about the village. “I couldn’t think of a more suitable person to renovate it.” Cllr Peter Gammons said it was a “very emotionally challenging thing” being faced with the possibility “it could collapse and be lost forever”. But, the Reform UK councillor, said this should “perhaps have been considered before buying it”. He said: “I don’t know that we can vote against the conservation officer on things which are regarded as being of historical importance. “But the other side of it is, we want to see this building preserved – we don’t want to see it lost.” The committee voted to approve the plans.

metadata.title: Fresh details on disgraced actor's criminal past emerge after death
metadata.contentSnippet: New details surrounding the criminal past of disgraced actor John Alford who sexually assaulted two teenage girls in Hertfordshire have emerged.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Fresh details on disgraced actor's criminal past emerge after death
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: New details surrounding the criminal past of a disgraced actor who sexually assaulted two teenage girls in Hertfordshire have emerged. Former London's Burning actor John Alford was jailed to eight and a half years in prison at St Albans Crown Court in January. The 54-year-old, of Holloway, north London, stood trial under his real name, John Shannon, in September last year. He was found guilty on four counts of sexual activity with the younger girl, and of sexual assault and assault by penetration on the older teenager. Born in Glasgow, Alford rose to fame as fireman Billy Ray in ITV drama London’s Burning in the 1990s. Alford was convicted six times for a total of 14 offences, documents reveal (Image: Jordan Pettitt) Unlocked using the Freedom of Information Act, the disgraced actor's criminal records have revealed new details of his criminal past. The former star of Grange Hill was convicted six times for a total of 14 offences, including "offences against property" and "public disorder". On May 26, 1999, Alford, appeared at at Snaresbrook Crown Court, in Redbridge, London, with supplying class A and class B drugs. Widely reported at the time, he was later found guilty of supplying cocaine and cannabis to an undercover News of the World reporter. Sentencing him at the same court, Judge Stephen Robbins imposed a nine-month prison sentence and ordered Alford to pay £3,000 in costs. On November 10, 2004, the star was convicted of using disorderly behaviour or threatening words "likely to cause harassment, alarm or distress". According to police records, the 54-year-old had booked into a hotel room with friends while in an "extremely drunken state" at 4am on October 10 that year. Alford's records reveal he "became loud and rowdy before causing damage to the room and contents when arrested for criminal damage". Alford's criminal records have been released using the Freedom of Information Act (Image: PA Media) He pleaded guilty at Cheltenham Magistrates' Court and fined £100 and ordered to pay £40 in costs. Less than two years later, on January 9, 2006, Alford was sentenced at Highbury Corner Magistrates' Court after admitting to drink driving. He was handed a 16-month driving ban after crashing his Rover into three cars in Islington, north London, on April 2 the previous year. Alford pleaded guilty to a minor road traffic offence which occurred on the same date and was fined £150 and ordered to pay £100 in costs. He next appeared at Highbury Corner Magistrates' Court on October 10, 2018, accused of smashing the window of a council bin lorry. He pleaded guilty to a charge of criminal damage but entered a not guilty plea to two counts of assault on a police officer. Alford later pleaded guilty to two counts of resisting an officer and was given a 12-month community order at a sentencing hearing on January 29, 2019. He was also ordered to pay a total of £400 in compensation, complete a rehabilitative activity and serve a curfew on an electronic tag. Born in Glasgow, Alford rose to fame as fireman Billy Ray in ITV drama London’s Burning (Image: Dominic Lipinski/PA Wire) Police records reveal Alford was also issued with two fixed penalty notices between December 2010 and 2017. The first was issued on December 2, 2010, after he was arrested on suspicion of being drunk and disorderly in a public place. The second was issued on September 7, 2017, when Alford was again arrested on suspicion of being drunk and disorderly. Officers were called to a McDonald's restaurant but the actor left the scene and was later "found by police nearby walking in the road, causing cars to swerve to avoid him". Alford was found unresponsive on his bed when staff opened his cell door at HMP Bure near Norwich and medics were called. Norfolk Coroner's Court opened an inquest into the death of the 54-year-old on June 16 with his provisional cause of death given as ischaemic heart disease. The Prisons and Probation Ombudsman confirmed it is conducting an independent investigation into the death. Alford was convicted six times for a total of 14 offences, documents reveal (Image: Jordan Pettitt) A spokesperson said: "We will make our final investigation report public after the inquest concludes." During his trial last year, the court heard Alford sexually assaulted the girls while they were drunk following a night out at the pub. The offences took place at the home of a third girl whose father was friends with Alford. The disgraced actor purchased £250 worth of food, alcohol and cigarettes from a petrol station in the early hours of the morning. Alford then had sexual intercourse with the 14-year-old girl in the garden and downstairs toilet of the home. He also inappropriately touched the 15-year-old girl as she lay half asleep on the living room sofa. Have you got a story you want to share? Get in touch at oliver.murphy@newsquest.co.uk

metadata.title: DWP new State Pension to rise almost £500 to more than £13,000 a year
metadata.contentSnippet: The State Pension is expected to rise by 3.9% next April, taking the full new payment to around £250.70 a week and more than £13,000 a year

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: DWP new State Pension to rise almost £500 to more than £13,000 a year
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Millions of State Pension recipients are on course for a pay rise next April, with the full new State Pension set to increase by nearly £490 over the year. The increase is 3.9% under the Triple Lock, after Chancellor John Healey confirmed the figures in his first Budget. This follows official figures from the Office for National Statistics (ONS), which showed average earnings growth of 3.9% between May and July. This was higher than September's Consumer Price Index (CPI) inflation rate of 3.5% and the Triple Lock's minimum increase of 2.5%. The Triple Lock means the State Pension rises each April by whichever is highest out of average earnings growth, inflation or 2.5%. The figures point to a weekly increase of £9.40 for people receiving the full new State Pension, taking payments from £241.30 to around £250.70. That would mean an extra £488.80 over a full year, with the annual payment rising from £12,547.60 to approximately £13,036.40. The full new State Pension would therefore pass £13,000 a year for the first time. But, it's important to say that pensioners aged 75 and over are on the older basic system of pension, which is still lower. The expected 3.9% increase would also apply to the full basic State Pension, paid to people who reached State Pension age before April 2016. The projected rates for the 2027/28 financial year are: Full new State Pension Full basic State Pension These figures are projections based on a 3.9% rise. The actual amounts will depend on the Government's formal uprating decision and rounding. It is important to remember that not everyone receives the full State Pension. The amount paid depends on an individual's National Insurance record and other entitlement rules. People are able to claim the new State Pension when they reach State Pension age if they are: Older pensioners get the basic State Pension, and some also get Additional State Pension. Recommended reading: Labour has pledged to maintain the Triple Lock for the duration of the current Parliament. Changes to the State Pension uprating system are scheduled to take effect from April 2030. The latest earnings figures mean the 2027 increase is expected to be driven by wage growth rather than inflation. September's CPI inflation rate was 3.5%, up from 3.1% in August. ONS chief economist Grant Fitzner said increased fuel prices were again the main driver, with diesel prices reaching their highest level since July 2022.

metadata.title: Cambridgeshire cat crisis worsens as RSPCA urges public to adopt or foster
metadata.contentSnippet: A growing 'cat crisis' has led to urgent calls for help in Cambridgeshire.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Cambridgeshire cat crisis worsens as RSPCA urges public to adopt or foster
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A growing 'cat crisis' has led to urgent calls for help in Cambridgeshire. The RSPCA says it is facing an all-time high in the number of cats needing care and launched an 'Adoptober' campaign to encourage more people to adopt or foster felines. Sally Jones, animal centre manager at RSPCA Block Fen, said: "We’ve seen a huge influx of cats and kittens at Block Fen. The animal welfare charity has warned of a “cat crisis” (Image: RSPCA) "Sadly it just isn’t slowing down – and it’s having a massive impact not just on us in Cambridgeshire but across England and Wales." So far this year, the Block Fen centre in Wimblington has taken in 53 cats, and the charity says cats are arriving faster than they can be rehomed. With hundreds of cats in national centres and thousands more housed in branches and private boarding facilities, space is running out. Sweet Matilda came to the RSPCA from a multi-cat household (Image: RSPCA) Ms Jones said: "We’re desperate for adopters and fosterers to come forward to help free up space in our centres. "This means we can help more cats rescued from cruelty and neglect, but also a cattery is not the ideal environment for cats and kittens and they can find it stressful, so getting them into a loving home as soon as we can is so much better for their overall welfare." Eight-year-old Spyhnx Charlie (Image: RSPCA) The RSPCA has named October 'Adoptober' and is appealing for members of the public to consider giving a rescue cat a second chance. The campaign comes as part of a wider effort to ease pressure on centres and improve animal welfare through rehoming. Turkey is around two years old (Image: RSPCA) Richard Hooker, Country Medical Director for inspiring vet care, said: "The number of unwanted and stray cats has reached unprecedented levels, making it even more important to ensure cats are neutered to prevent unwanted litters of kittens putting even more pressure on charities." To rehome a cat from Block Fen, visit the RSPCA website and complete an online application form.

metadata.title: Cambs Mayor calls for funding control after Autumn Budget
metadata.contentSnippet: The Mayor of Cambridgeshire and Peterborough has called for more local control over funding following the Autumn Budget.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Cambs Mayor calls for funding control after Autumn Budget
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: The Mayor of Cambridgeshire and Peterborough has called for more local control over funding following the Autumn Budget. Paul Bristow, the Mayor of Cambridgeshire and Peterborough, shared his views on the Autumn Budget for 2026, emphasising the importance of increased mayoral control over funds for regional growth. He acknowledged some disagreements with the budget but welcomed the decision to designate the Cambridge Biomedical Campus as a special zone for business rates. He stated: "Making the Cambridge Biomedical Campus a special zone for Business Rates will help our region as it expands." The campus, which contributes £4.7 billion annually to the UK economy, is expected to further boost local infrastructure and job creation. Mr Bristow criticised the current system where areas generating growth must seek resources from Whitehall, advocating for preemptive investments to manage rising demands. He also found the proposed Good Growth Fund and new borrowing powers promising, aiming for long-term infrastructure-led development. His focus remains on ensuring that regional growth benefits local residents, vowing to collaborate with the Greater Cambridge Development Corporation on the new measures.

metadata.title: WATCH: Court shown CCTV that ‘captures knife attacker on LNER train’
metadata.contentSnippet: CCTV footage shows a knifeman on a London-bound train where he stabbed 10 people, a court heard.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: WATCH: Court shown CCTV that ‘captures knife attacker on LNER train’
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: CCTV footage shows a knifeman on an LNER train that made an emergency stop in Huntingdon where he stabbed 10 people, a court heard. Prosecutor Christopher Paxton KC told Cambridge Crown Court that Anthony Williams "brought terror" to the Doncaster to London LNER service, stabbing 10 people during a "rampage" on November 1 last year. Several people were injured on an LNER train from Doncaster to London King's Cross on November 1, 2025 which was forced to make an emergency stop in Huntingdon. Anthony Williams, 33, denies 14 counts of attempted murder: ten of them in relation to the LNER train, three said to have happened in Peterborough and one at Pontoon Dock DLR station in London. Earlier this month, Williams pleaded guilty to 10 counts of wounding with intent relating to the incident on the LNER train, the wounding with intent of a man at Pontoon Dock DLR station in the early hours of November 1 and to the wounding with intent of a 14-year-old boy in Peterborough on October 31, as well as a number of other offences. His trial opened at Cambridge Crown Court on October 28. In footage played to jurors on Wednesday, a knifeman, dressed in a black hoodie, trousers and cap, is seen walking down the aisle of the LNER train before producing the knife. Jurors also saw footage of passenger Stephen Crean attempting to wrestle the knife from Williams. Another passenger, Jonathan Gjoshe, boarded the London-bound train at Doncaster before he saw a man dressed all in black pull out a knife, prosecutor Christopher Paxton KC told jurors. Mr Gjoshe believed Williams was following him and told other passengers: “Please make sure he's not following me”, the court heard. Jurors heard that Mr Gjoshe screamed at other passengers: “Just run, just run, there’s a guy with a knife. I’ve been stabbed. I’ve been stabbed”. Mr Paxton told the court that Mr Gjoshe asked medics: “Am I going to die today or not?” when he was taken to hospital after the attack. The trial continues.
